text:
ConocoPhillips edged up 0.23% today to $137.35, capping a strong two-week rally of 6% that accelerated over the past few days. The modest daily gain reflects the oil market itself: while U.S. crude fell slightly Friday, it remains elevated at $97 a barrel, supported by a week of geopolitical shocks in the Middle East—Saudi Arabia's shutdown of its East-West pipeline after drone attacks, and Houthi advances toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments. As a major oil and gas producer, ConocoPhillips benefits when crude prices stay high and supply concerns mount.

The two-week rally has coincided with escalating Middle East tensions that keep oil prices well above their summer levels, even as short-term volatility and profit-taking pull prices back on individual days like today. The company's steady climb reflects investor expectations that geopolitical risk premiums will persist in the oil market.
